Exact scope and earlier findings

Partial snapshot, failed/interrupted publication, overlap with/without a predecessor, SIGKILL recovery refusal and successful cleanup retain the previously reviewed fail-closed behavior. Verify-only access/readback, canonical merge/replace semantics, stdin/inherited-pipe secret flow and macOS Bash 3.2 compatibility remain intact. Validation and preservation
Inspected claude-repair2-result.json and actual repair2-logs/test-keys-backup.log and agentic-validate.log. The targeted log states "# tests 26", "# pass 26", "# fail 0". The gate actually runs test:keys-backup, lockfile check, lint:strict, typecheck:all, secrets scan, cross-agent check, docs check, roadmap check and build; it ends "Agentic validation gate passed." and "Tests run: test:keys-backup", with recorded exit 0. It reports 20 checked shell files, 210 checked Markdown files and the repository secret scan passing for 4,941 files. Build warnings are present; this approval does not relabel the output warning-free. These are inspected execution artifacts, not tests run by this reviewer.
Read repair2-preservation-verification.json and independently compared immutable main/final blobs: dependency lockfiles/.npmrc, reviewer configuration, verdict/closeout/CI/auto-merge machinery, dependency policy/age gates and desktop-build-full orchestrator are preserved exactly. Version stays 2.25.147; every existing main package script and targeted-suite mapping is preserved, with additive backup test routing. The source-map main fix is retained. No review or validation control was weakened to obtain this conclusion.

Honest residual limits
No real Keychain, installed app, backup/restore, age/gpg/OpenSSL or user secrets were exercised. The age/OpenSSL flows use isolated stubs; OpenSSL fixtures compute real HMAC-SHA256 over marker/base64 ciphertext and use deterministic barriers/failure stubs, so they validate script control/publication contracts rather than production cipher interoperability. Gpg fixture coverage remains absent and is disclosed, not claimed. The existing disclosed OpenSSL HMAC passphrase-in-argv exception remains; key-value argv protection does not mean every encryption passphrase is absent from argv. The two-file publication is not literally atomic: the reviewed guarantee is recoverability/preservation of a complete prior pair and cleanup ownership. SIGKILL/power-loss leaves a lock/kept pair requiring explicit manual recovery; no automatic takeover is promised. Real iCloud/APFS behavior and real cryptographic/tool interoperability were not measured.
Shared node_modules were reused and are disclosed as stale relative to main's dependency fixes. The affected key fixtures use Node built-ins and isolated stubs; the recorded broader gate passes describe that actual environment and do not claim a fresh npm-ci reproduction or CI completion. No fresh dependency-install claim is made. The approved validation document lists real dry-run/backup/verify checks for Bradley "manual, when convenient"; they remain unperformed recommendations, not an invented pre-merge human gate. No external-provider behavior was introduced here, so no live provider response proof is claimed or needed for this change. These retained limits do not expose an additional blocking defect in the authorized reviewed scope.

Model and operational controls
Supported configuration: GPT-6.1 Sol (gpt-6.1-sol), medium reasoning, single independent reviewer, fork_turns none, no delegation; this is configuration evidence, not independently attested runtime identity. Only immutable Git/source and existing local evidence were inspected, including read-only hashes/metadata checks. No behavior tests, production/native/crypto/credential/network operations, worktree edits, Claude communication, publication, verdict recording or merge were performed. Only this requested actual final conclusion file is written. Both authorized automatic repair cycles have been assessed; no third repair cycle is proposed and no earlier finding is dropped. Any later code change requires a fresh SHA-pinned review.
